subject: Acme POC kickoff - recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Peters <john.peters@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC kickoff - recap & next steps

John / team,

Thanks again for a great kickoff earlier today. Quick recap to make sure we’re aligned and to surface the immediate next steps.

High-level goals
- Reduce latency on key customer-facing embeddings/search path from ~350ms to <150ms at 95th percentile
- Cut per-token inference cost on assistant routes by ~40% while preserving answer quality
- Pilot Redwood’s private deployment options for sensitive logs/data (non-PII)

Pain points you reiterated
- Current provider’s tail latency under load causes user-facing timeouts
- Engineering overhead to manage quantized models and batching
- Need for clearer cost forecasting for monthly spend

Scope for the pilot / POC (proposed)
- 4-week technical POC scoped to: 1) inference latency/throughput benchmarking on a sample workload, 2) cost comparison with live traffic profile, 3) quality checks on a prioritized prompt set (search + FAQ bot)
- Benchmarks: 95p latency, tokens/s throughput at steady-state, and per-token cost delta vs current provider
- Owner (Redwood): Aditya Rao (runtime lead) — responsible for setup, kernel tuning, and results
- Owner (Acme): John Peters — provide sample prompt set, representative traffic trace, and access to test environment

Prompt set & evals
- We’ll start with the 50 canonical prompts you mentioned and add 10 failure cases (timeouts/long-tail).
- Evaluation criteria: exact-match for structured responses, BLEU and human-grade QA for open answers. We’ll share a lightweight eval harness and results dashboard.

Timeline / milestones
- Week 0 (this week): access & infra checklist, config kickoff
- Week 1: model onboarding and baseline benchmark (current provider)
- Week 2: Redwood config, kernel/quantization tuning
- Week 3: production-like load run and evals
- Week 4: results review & decision point (scale or iterate)

Access/setup steps (action items)
- Acme: share sample prompt set, S3 test traces, and temporary test credentials (API key or service account) — OWNER: John
- Redwood: send infra checklist + terraform + test harness — OWNER: Aditya
- Both: schedule 30m sync on Mon Nov 2 to review access (I’ll send a meeting invite)

Attachments
- redwood-poc-scope.pdf (POC scope & success metrics)
- access-checklist.md (infrastructure access checklist)

Next steps
1) John — share prompt set and sample traces by Mon (11/2)
2) Aditya — send infra checklist + initial config by Tue (11/3)
3) I’ll create the HubSpot record and loop in Sales Ops for procurement

If I missed anything or you want different success metrics, say so and I’ll update.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0134
From: John Peters <john.peters@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Acme POC kickoff - recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks right to me. Appreciate the concise summary.

I’ll get the 50 prompt set and a trimmed traffic trace to you by end of day Monday (11/2). I’m also looping in our procurement lead, Sara Liu (sara.liu@acme.com), to start the contracting conversation.

A couple quick clarifications:
- For the baseline run, we can provide a 48-hour trace exported from our staging cluster — should that be sufficient?
- On the privacy side: we need to ensure logs are configurable to avoid PII retention during the pilot. Is that supported out of the box?

Thanks,
John
